connections.observation: `s001` marks descent (κατέβην) into the Piraeus; `s005` shows that the initial homeward direction (πρὸς τὸ ἄστυ, οἴκαδε) is reversed so that οἴκαδε later names arrival at Polemarchus' house. Held together, they make visible a spatial inversion: descent leads not to return upward but to a second οἴκαδε deeper within the Piraeus.

`s013` concentrates three forms of κελεύω (command) in the relay from Polemarchus through the slave; `s003` shows περιμένω (to wait) passing through the same relay and accumulating in the exchange. Together they make visible a chain of transmission in which both command and its content are relayed through successive speakers.

`s006` frames the situation as a disjunction of force (κρείττους γένεσθε) or staying; `s007` makes number visible as the ground of that force (ὁράτε ὅσοι ἐσμέν); `s004` contrasts persuasion (πείσωμεν) with not listening (μὴ ἀκούοντας, μὴ ἀκουσομένων). Held together, they make visible the replacement of speech by number: persuasion is foreclosed by a refusal to listen grounded in superior force.

`s014` states prayer (προσευξόμενός) as a purpose and then completes it (προσευξάμενοι); `s002` shows θεάσασθαι as the initial purpose of descent, which returns later as θεάσασθαι and θεασόμεθα in Polemarchus' inducement. Together they make visible a pattern where stated purposes are completed (prayer) or displaced and repeated (viewing).

`s008` introduces the torch relay on horseback (λαμπάδια ἔχοντες διαδώσουσιν ἀλλήλοις ἁμιλλώμενοι τοῖς ἵπποις), a relay of passing; `s009` projects a temporal sequence (μετὰ τὸ δεῖπνον ... τὴν παννυχίδα θεασόμεθα) extending through the night. Held together, they make visible the future festival as a combination of relay-movement and nocturnal duration.

`s017` sequences seeing from a distance (κατιδὼν πόρρωθεν), turning around (μετεστράφην), and approach from behind (ὄπισθεν προσέρχεται); `s012` shows the slave running (δραμόντα) and then grasping from behind (ὄπισθεν λαβόμενος τοῦ ἱματίου). Together they make visible a spatial choreography in which Socrates is seen, turned toward, approached from behind, and physically detained from behind.

`s011` marks Cephalus as very old (μάλα πρεσβύτης) and unseen for a long time (διὰ χρόνου); `s010` shows him seated, garlanded, having just sacrificed (ἐστεφανωμένος, τεθυκώς). Held together, they make visible the conjunction of age, temporal distance, and ritual completion in Cephalus' first appearance.

`s015` contrasts two processions—the local one fine (καλὴ ἡ τῶν ἐπιχωρίων πομπὴ) and the Thracian one no less fitting (οὐ μέντοι ἧττον ἐφαίνετο πρέπειν ἣν οἱ Θρᾷκες ἔπεμπον); `s002` shows θεάσασθαι as the purpose of viewing the procession's manner (τίνα τρόπον ποιήσουσιν). Together they make visible that the stated purpose of viewing leads to a comparative judgment between two performances.

`s016` shows μένω moving from Polemarchus' disjunction (μένετ᾽ αὐτοῦ) to his direct command (μένετε) to Glaucon's acceptance of necessity (μενετέον); `s004` shows persuasion (πείσωμεν) proposed by Socrates and refused by Polemarchus through the figure of not listening (μὴ ἀκούοντας). Together they make visible the conversion of a disjunction into a completed imperative after persuasion is foreclosed.

`s003` shows περιμένω relayed from Polemarchus through the slave to Socrates and Glaucon, accumulating across speakers; `s008` describes torch-bearers passing torches to one another in relay (λαμπάδια ἔχοντες διαδώσουσιν ἀλλήλοις). Held together, the two relay sequences—one of command and waiting, one of torches on horseback—make visible a doubled figure of mediated transmission.

elements.context: κατιδὼν οὖν πόρρωθεν ἡμᾶς οἴκαδε ὡρμημένους

new_signals.observation: Polemarchus sees Socrates and Glaucon from a distance (πόρρωθεν) before the slave is sent to detain them—a spatial separation that initiates the relay of command.

elements.context: ἐξαναστησόμεθα γὰρ μετὰ τὸ δεῖπνον καὶ τὴν παννυχίδα θεασόμεθα

new_signals.observation: Rising (ἐξαναστησόμεθα) after dinner marks a future threshold between the meal and the nocturnal viewing—a projected movement within the temporal sequence of the festival.

elements.form: συνεσόμεθά τε πολλοῖς τῶν νέων αὐτόθι καὶ διαλεξόμεθα
elements.context: καὶ συνεσόμεθά τε πολλοῖς τῶν νέων αὐτόθι καὶ διαλεξόμεθα

new_signals.observation: Polemarchus projects being together (συνεσόμεθα) with many young men and conversing (διαλεξόμεθα) as part of the nocturnal festival—two future social actions named alongside viewing.

elements.context: ἔκειντο γὰρ δίφροι τινὲς αὐτόθι κύκλῳ

new_signals.observation: Chairs arranged in a circle (δίφροι κύκλῳ) are found in the courtyard where Cephalus has sacrificed—a spatial configuration that receives the arriving group.
